html:
The Kinsey Institute is a research centre for sex, gender and reproduction at Indiana University in Bloomington. Alfred Kinsey founded it in 1947 as the Institute for Sex Research.

Kinsey, a zoologist who first studied gall wasps, began collecting sex histories in 1938 after he was asked to teach a marriage course. The students' questions showed how little reliable data existed. By 1940 he was pressed to give up either the course or his interviews, and he chose the research. His funds came from the university and, from 1941, from the Rockefeller Foundation through a committee of the National Research Council led by the psychologist Robert Yerkes.

In 1947 he set the work on a firm base as a non-profit institute. It produced the Kinsey Reports of 1948 and 1953. Funding from the Rockefeller Foundation stopped in 1954. Kinsey died in 1956 and the Institute went on without him. It holds a large library and archive and is still active today under a longer name.
sum: The Kinsey Institute is a research centre for sex, gender and reproduction at Indiana University in Bloomington. Alfred Kinsey founded it in 1947 as the Institute for Sex Research.
